You can choose the Titicaca Train instead of the bus. The supplement is $295 per person; the train departs on Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays according to the operator's timetable.

The railway crosses the high Andes, plateaus and valleys. The train has a dining car, a bar car and a panoramic carriage. A stop at La Raya, at an altitude of more than 4,300 meters, allows you to admire the mountain peaks and plains.

The price includes a lunch of a starter, main course and dessert. Arrival in Puno is at around 19:00, followed by a transfer and check-in at the hotel.

The floating Uros Islands were built by local residents using totora reeds that grow in the lake. During the visit, guests will discover the traditional way of life of the Uros people, learn how the islands and reed houses are constructed, and see traditional boats and locally made crafts.

The journey then continues to Taquile Island, known for its picturesque scenery, terraced slopes and rich cultural heritage. The islanders of Taquile preserve distinctive traditions, and their textile art is inscribed on UNESCO's list of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. During the walk, you can enjoy panoramic views of the lake and learn about the life of local communities.

## Tijuca: A Vast Tropical Forest in Rio

The forest contains Tijuca Peak, 1,021 meters high, with panoramic views over Rio de Janeiro. The forest surrounds the famous Christ the Redeemer statue. Hundreds of species of plants and animals live here, including monkeys, toucans, sloths, coatis and many species of butterflies and birds.

Tijuca Forest is the world's largest urban tropical forest, covering around 32 square kilometers on mountain slopes within the city of Rio de Janeiro. It is also one of the city's most impressive ecological success stories. During the 18th and early 19th centuries, much of the original forest was cleared for coffee and sugarcane plantations. As Rio de Janeiro grew, water shortages became an increasingly pressing problem, and in the 1860s Emperor Pedro II ordered the start of a large-scale reforestation project. Over the following decades, the Atlantic Forest gradually reclaimed this area, turning it into the thriving ecosystem visitors can enjoy today.

Departure in the morning. A scenic road through mountains and pine forests takes us to Tlaxcala.
The first stop is the Sanctuary of San Miguel del Milagro, where the Archangel Michael appeared to Diego Lázaro in 1631. Holy Mass will be celebrated here.
We then continue to Tlaxcala, founded by the Spanish between 1519 and 1524, and visit San Francisco Monastery.
Next we visit the Sanctuary of Our Lady of Ocotlán, one of the most striking examples of Baroque architecture in the region. It is considered one of the most important religious centers in Mexico.
The centerpiece of the complex is the Camerín, where the statue of the Virgin Mary is dressed for important religious ceremonies. At the main altar, we will see a beautifully preserved image of the Virgin Mary, which, according to tradition, miraculously appeared on a tree.


The journey continues to Puebla, located in a broad valley surrounded by mountains and volcanoes: Popocatépetl, Iztaccíhuatl, La Malinche and Pico de Orizaba.
Puebla was founded in 1531 and was one of the most important cities of the colonial period. The city's architectural significance led to its historic center being inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List.
In the city, we will see the cathedral, one of Puebla's most outstanding buildings, along with the Rosary Chapel and Santo Domingo Church.
Return to Mexico City.
